children: Enterprise software and cloud major Oracle Corp. (ORCL, Financials) just offered investors a far sharper view of what AI is doing to its business.
Oracle shares jumped nearly 7% in after-hours trading on better-than-expected first-quarter fiscal results and an upbeat outlook.
Cloud sales up 62% year over year. And that's where the story gets interesting.
Oracle has invested heavily in building data centers and computing power for AI customers. Investors had been watching the spending for some time. And now they're starting to see the benefits.
The company booked over $30 billion in new AI cloud contracts during the quarter, giving it more business to sort through in the coming months.
Oracle also forecasts revenue growth of 30% to 34% for the second quarter and adjusted earnings of $1.85 to $1.93 a share.
That's not the kind of growth rate investors used to associate with Oracle. But there is a fly in the ointment.
AI infrastructure isn't cheap and the company has to keep converting those contracts into revenue, while not allowing capital expenditures to eat into cash flow.
That's what investors care about next. Oracle has already proven it can win big AI business. Now it has to prove those deals can translate into profitable, sustainable development.

title: Oracle Just Dropped an AI Number Wall Street Cannot Ignore
